title: Request Storage Conservation Demo - SaltBay Analytics
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood request storage/conservation controls in Console + API. Covered per-route toggles, real-time redaction rules, PII detectors, KMS integration, and a proposed 1-week pilot to validate retention and performance. Customer asked about audit trail, SSO/KMS, and fallback behavior for hosted vs private. Agreed next steps: send security pack, provide sandbox, pricing estimate for 50k req/day pilot.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2028-01-17
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Product), Jonah Lee (Redwood Solutions), Evan Marks (SaltBay), Ritu Patel (SaltBay Sec), Omar Kahn (SaltBay ML), Lina Zhou (SaltBay Proc)

Auto-generated summary: demo focused on storage toggles + PII redaction.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood, ill kick off, we have diego and priya with me, quick agenda - console toggles, api flags, redaction rules, q&a.
00:19 Speaker 2 (Evan): thanks maya, appreciate it. we are primarily evaluating how to keep sensitive fields out of logs and to control retention per route. latency matters but we can't keep raw PII.
00:37 Speaker 3 (Diego): great, quick heads up — i'll share my screen and walk the console. the first thing to call out is per-route request-storage settings; you can set three modes: persist, ephemeral, or policy-managed.
01:05 Speaker 4 (Ritu): when you say ephemeral, is that truly non-persistent or just short TTL? we need assurance for audit trail too.
01:18 Speaker 3 (Diego): ephemeral is a non-persist option where request payloads are not written to long-term object store; transient KV remains for prompt caching only and evicted. audit metadata (request id, timestamp, decision) is kept in the audit log with hashed pointers, not the raw content. note: we can optionally increase audit retention for compliance.
01:46 Speaker 2 (Evan): can you show the regex-based redaction? our data has lots of free text, so heuristics matter.
01:55 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes. in the console under Security -> Redaction you can add rules. by default we ship heuristics for emails, ssns, phone numbers, and a named-entity PII model. you can add regex overrides per-route. watch this — i'll add a sample rule to redact pattern that looks like "cust_id_[0-9]{6}".
02:30 Speaker 5 (Omar): do you support entity-level redaction for JSON keys? e.g., keep the non-sensitive fields but redact values for key = 'ssn' ?
02:41 Speaker 3 (Diego): yep, we have JSON path support. you can do path-based redaction: $.user.ssn -> redact. we also support structured extraction so if you want to keep the name but redact the id, that's possible.
03:05 Speaker 1 (Maya): a couple product notes, you can also choose 'tokenized mask' where the model receives masked tokens to preserve semantic shape but remove identifiers — that helps with model quality while protecting PII.
03:28 Speaker 4 (Ritu): how does key management work? our legal requires HSM-backed KMS, and we need to rotate keys quarterly.
03:39 Speaker 3 (Diego): we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and also with external HSM via our private deployment connector. rotations are supported; you can bring-your-own-key and we keep key access logs. i'll show the KMS config tab.
04:10 Speaker 6 (Priya): one nuance — for hosted customers we manage envelope encryption but you can request that keys never leave your control via a private deployment. that tends to be the ask for regulated industries.
04:35 Speaker 2 (Evan): timeline question — if we start a pilot, what is the rollback behavior if a route misconfig is applied and blocks traffic?
04:47 Speaker 3 (Diego): there are safe defaults and an automatic rollback policy. you can set a canary rule: apply to 5% traffic, watch metrics, then ramp. if errors spike the route goes back to previous config and we notify via webhook or slack integration.
05:10 Speaker 5 (Omar): about costs — will ephemeral mode save token-storage fees?
05:17 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, ephemeral reduces storage-related billing rows, and Optimize will recommend batching and cache TTLs to further cut per-token costs. we can run a quick cost sim once you share traffic shape.
05:40 Speaker 3 (Diego): i'm switching to the API now. two flags you can set on requests: x-redwood-storage: ephemeral|persist|policy and x-redwood-redact: auto|none|custom. examples in SDK snippet in the doc.
06:05 Speaker 2 (Evan): can the SDK toggle be set per-call as a header? we need dynamic behavior — sometimes risk scoring routes require longer retention.
06:16 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes per-call header works or you can bind policy to route id and let the app-level router choose route.
06:40 Speaker 4 (Ritu): audit logs — what fields are kept? we need user id, request id, timestamp, decision and operator. we cannot keep the raw prompt.
06:52 Speaker 3 (Diego): audit retains metadata: request id, route id, timestamp, retention decision (ephemeral/persist), redact rules applied, and the hashed content fingerprint. the raw content only persists if policy==persist.
07:20 Speaker 5 (Omar): any support for schema-based masking? our payloads are strict JSON.
07:28 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes — schema-driven masking is available; you upload a schema and mark sensitive fields and mask will run server-side.
07:44 Speaker 6 (Priya): i'll call out Optimize's role — our Optimize engine suggests which routes could safely move to ephemeral or tokenized mask based on historical semantic drift and quality regressions. it can simulate the quality delta using held-out evals.
08:05 Speaker 2 (Evan): interesting, how accurate are those sims? we have tight quality SLOs.
08:13 Speaker 6 (Priya): medium to high accuracy for surface-level prompts; for domain-specific jargon we recommend a short retest. Optimize surfaces a predicted quality loss score and confidence band.
08:35 Speaker 3 (Diego): demoing the redaction rule log now — you can preview a sample request and see which tokens would be redacted; note that NER sometimes flags company names as entities, so you may need to tune.
09:02 Speaker 4 (Ritu): any false positives concern — we can't redact things that break downstream parsing.
09:12 Speaker 3 (Diego): we log redaction hits and let you configure post-redaction validators. you can opt to keep a sanitized copy under restricted access for debugging.
09:36 Speaker 2 (Evan): let's talk compliance packages — does Redwood support SOC2 Type II and ISO?
09:44 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO27001; i'll send the pack. for certain customers we do additional attestations as part of private deployment.
10:00 Speaker 5 (Omar): latency impact — does redaction happen inline or async?
10:07 Speaker 3 (Diego): default is inline for path-based redaction (minimal added latency ~5-15ms). heavier NER-based redaction runs in a microservice and adds slightly more; inline vs async is configurable per-route.
10:30 Speaker 6 (Priya): tradeoff note: inline redaction preserves single-call semantics, async can be used if you can tolerate eventual sanitation.
11:00 Speaker 2 (Evan): ok can you show the policy-managed mode?
11:07 Speaker 3 (Diego): policy-managed is where you attach a policy set that uses signalers (risk score, user tier, data classification) to choose retention dynamically. i'll flip to that screen.
11:40 Speaker 4 (Ritu): for legal we need key rotation logs and proof that keys were not used after rotation date.
11:48 Speaker 3 (Diego): rotation events are recorded in the audit trail with key fingerprints; plus we provide attestation logs for rotations.
12:05 Speaker 5 (Omar): question on backups — if ephemeral is chosen, are there any backup snapshots that might include data?
12:14 Speaker 3 (Diego): ephemeral mode excludes payloads from backups. backups only include config and audit metadata. we also have an ejection process to remove any transient backups.
12:40 Speaker 2 (Evan): let's talk about the pilot: we want to test 50k req/day for 7 days across three routes, verify no material quality loss and that retention tooling blocks PII.
12:56 Speaker 1 (Maya): perfect — proposed success criteria: <1% regression on eval prompts, zero PII leakage in sample set, and stability under 95th pct latency SLO.
13:18 Speaker 4 (Ritu): who gets access to the sanitized debug copies? must be RBAC enforced.
13:26 Speaker 6 (Priya): RBAC is integrated with SSO (SAML/Okta). you can grant ephemeral debug access to a limited group and all accesses are logged.
13:50 Speaker 5 (Omar): are there hooks for SIEM? we use Splunk.
13:57 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes webhook + syslog + Splunk forwarder. we also expose an events API for streaming audit log.
14:20 Speaker 2 (Evan): procurement question — for the pilot what billing look like?
14:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll send a pilot estimate; typically pilots are usage-priced with a small committed credit. i'll follow up.
14:45 Speaker 4 (Lina): contract and DPA — do you have a standard DPA?
14:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes standard DPA, plus addenda for EU/UK data residency, we'll attach.
15:05 Speaker 5 (Omar): a little nit — the term "K V cache" in docs is confusing, some engs read it as key value cache and others as K V token.
15:16 Speaker 3 (Diego): noted — we call it KV (key-value) cache; docs updated.
15:30 Speaker 2 (Evan): any known limitations on private deployment for schema-based redaction?
15:37 Speaker 3 (Diego): private supports all redaction features; some integrations (managed KMS short-path) differ. we'll put matrix in the security doc.
16:00 Speaker 6 (Priya): quick demo wrap — i'm going to create a demo script for the sandbox that hits persist and ephemeral routes and shows redaction events.
16:12 Speaker 1 (Maya): cool. open Q's?
16:18 Speaker 2 (Evan): one last on data residency — can we restrict storage to eu-west-1 and have audit logs mirrored to our splunk in london?
16:28 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes regional storage plus log forwarding to your Splunk; we'll note network peering and egress.
16:44 Speaker 4 (Ritu): sounds good. please include the egress and peering notes in the security packet.
16:52 Speaker 1 (Maya): recap and next steps: i'll send security pack + DPA, diego will spin up sandbox, evan will share prompts, we schedule pilot kickoff. thanks all.

End transcript.
